transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-06 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Morales (Redwood CSM); Aisha Karim (Summit ML Lead), Tom Reynolds (Product), Javier Ortiz (Security)

Summary (auto): quick recap at top, see action items below

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Aisha Karim: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:08] Liam Park: Morning all, Liam here, I'll start with the eval results - pulled from the nightly run.
[00:15] Tom Reynolds: Quick note, we had some folks pull in from engineering but they couldn't make the time today.
[00:22] Liam Park: Cool. So to the results: overall pass rate is 87% on the baseline prompt set A, but prompt set B dropped to 68% after applying the INT8 quant profile; the regression looks concentrated on the compliance phrasing and monetary formatting cases.
[00:40] Aisha Karim: Interesting, we saw that too in our internal check. Is that the KV cache change you mentioned last week?
[00:49] Liam Park: Might be related — the quantization + kernel reorder can change tokenization edge cases, also the reranker threshold we used was slightly lower. There's some transcription issues in logs so I'm gonna attach the raw latencies.
[01:05] Maya Chen: We'll drop the thresholds for the reranker and re-run. Also, can you point to a couple concrete examples of the fail cases?
[01:12] Liam Park: Sure, for example prompt B-12 - customer ID formatting. Model returned 'acct 123-4' instead of 'acct-1234', and in another case the guardrail filter flagged an allowed PII token as sensitive because of tokenization split.
[01:28] Aisha Karim: Yeah that exact PII false positive is blocking our compliance signoff, so we need to retune pronto.
[01:36] Sofia Morales: Noted, I'll flag security as a blocker in the notes.
[01:40] Javier Ortiz: For security perspective, we need to see the KMS flow and an excerpt of SOC2, also retention for logs.
[01:48] Maya Chen: We'll share the SOC2 excerpt by tomorrow, Sofia will own.
[01:52] [crosstalk] Tom Reynolds: Also, any change to the prompt template — we prefer minimal edits so product doesn't have to rework UI.
[02:00] Liam Park: Agreed. I propose we try two adjustments: one, add a short deterministic post-processing step for numeric and account formatting; two, bump the reranker threshold from 0.55 to 0.62 for those templates. That should restore precision without hurting recall much.
[02:20] Aisha Karim: Sounds reasonable. Can you quantify the expected delta?
[02:24] Liam Park: On our dev rig we saw precision improve by ~9 points and recall drop ~2 points on set B, net F1 up by ~5. But that's on small sample — need the dedicated infra run for confidence.
[02:36] Maya Chen: Okay next, on scoring — we propose an updated rubric: classify into Critical/High/Acceptable, with thresholds 0-0.5, 0.5-0.75, 0.75-1.0 respectively. That maps to pass/fail for automations.
[02:52] Tom Reynolds: Would love that as a column in the shared sheet.
[02:56] Maya Chen: We'll add it. Link to sheet: drive.google.com/open?id=sheet-eval-834 (note: placeholder)
[03:05] [00:03:15] Liam Park: On guardrails, we also found two false positives in the semantic filter when the text included legal sample phrases like 'for internal use only' — the filter treated 'internal' as sensitive. We'll tune the regex and model-based classifier.
[03:30] Aisha Karim: Any impact on latency? Our SLO is 350ms p95.
[03:35] Liam Park: On hosted it's 300-350ms p95 for these prompt lengths; on dedicated with batching we currently see 220-260ms p95. The quantized model ran slightly faster but introduced those edge regressions.
[03:50] Maya Chen: So the tradeoff is clear: quantized gains in latency/cost but some accuracy regressions. For the POC, you said cost sensitivity is medium — which direction do you want to prioritize?
[04:02] Tom Reynolds: We want a balance; cost matters but we can't accept compliance misses. So prefer conservative tuning — keep accuracy first.
[04:10] Aisha Karim: Agreed. Let's keep hosted quantized for non-sensitive flows and dedicated FP16 for compliance-critical paths.
[04:18] Liam Park: We can route by policy — latency-sensitive calls to quantized hosted with checksum fallbacks; sensitive calls to dedicated FP16 pool. We'll prototype route config.
[04:30] Maya Chen: Great. Action items — to confirm: Liam will run full regression on dedicated infra and share logs; Maya sends updated eval sheet and new thresholds; Aisha provides 3 extra prompts; Sofia shares SOC2 excerpt and KMS flow.
[04:48] Aisha Karim: I'll add those prompts by Sunday.
[04:52] Javier Ortiz: I'll review SOC2 stub once Sofia shares.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Any blockers on scheduling the canary rollout? 2026-05-14 work?
[04:59] Tom Reynolds: That works on our end, pending the regression pass.
[05:04] Liam Park: I'll also include a perf script so you can reproduce locally.
[05:08] [End of recording]
